resources.string: Foreign text on the screen is read in any app; its translation shows at the bottom, like a film\'s subtitles. Text already in the language you translate into, and apps\' buttons, are skipped. When Android asks, share the entire screen. Latin and Chinese letters are read.
For the phone\'s sound Android asks to share the screen. Hammurabi only listens; it takes no pictures of the screen.
Add a Hammurabi switch to Quick Settings
Hammurabi is in Quick Settings: pull down from the top of the screen to turn it on in any app.
Add it by hand: open Quick Settings, tap the pencil, and drag Hammurabi in.
The first time, the translation model downloads (%s; Wi-Fi recommended).
Tiny keeps up on most phones. Base hears better but needs a fast phone.
Takes effect when the app starts again.
What is heard or read is recognized and translated on this phone; neither sound nor pictures of the screen leave it. The models download once, from Hugging Face.
To show captions over a video, allow Hammurabi to display over other apps.
Hammurabi needs the microphone permission to listen.
Without screen sharing, neither the screen nor the phone\'s sound can be translated.
Tap to open, or stop here.
